source: We propose a novel method to sparsify attention in the Transformer model by learning to select the most-informative token representations , thus leveraging the model's information bottleneck with twofold strength. A careful analysis shows that the contextualization of encoded representations in our model is significantly more effective than in the original Transformer. We achieve a notable reduction in memory usage due to an improved differentiable top-k operator , making the model suitable to process long documents, as shown on an example of a summarization task .
target: We propose a novel method to sparsify attention in the Transformer model by learning to select the most-informative token representations during the training process, thus focusing on task-specific parts of the input. reason: Adds a quadratic-to-sublinear complexity claim not asserted in the source.
